thread:
Devon: quick handoff note — saw a couple of alerts during my shift, booking them in the runbook. One Q: who should be paged when throughput drops ~40% across a dedicated pool? SRE or Runtime?

Maria: short answer: depends on root cause. If it's infra (GPU health, network, host OOMs) -> SRE. If it's model-serving (KV cache pressure, batching gone wrong, model OOM on a container) -> Runtime. If unknown, page SRE first and they can call runtime if it's at layer 7.

Devon: can we get a concrete paging matrix? sometimes folks hesitate and we end up with slow noisy alerts.

Lee: +1. Proposed quick matrix:
- Sev1 (complete outage / >90% customers impacted): page both SRE and Runtime, escalate to Sam (EM).
- Sev2 (degraded latency/throughput with functional fallbacks, ~20-80% impact): page owning team (SRE for infra, Runtime for model-serving) + optionally notify other team in slack thread.
- Sev3 (minor increase in error-rate or internal queueing, <20%): create ticket and notify on-call via thread, no immediate page.

Maria: adding some signal checks to decide routing: p95 latency, node health (drain/oom), host CPU/GPU steal, container restarts. If p95 latency jumps but hosts look fine -> runtime. If node restart率 or GPU ECC errors -> SRE.

Devon: thanks. what about model-quality regressions (e.g., hallucination spike / soft-failure in generation)? who declares 'incident' there?

Lee: Runtime owns model output quality and evals, so runtime triages. If we detect production-facing quality regression that causes customer-visible incorrect responses (esp. compliance/regulatory impact) -> declare incident and page Product + SRE if infrastructure is implicated. Example: generation suddenly includes PII or banned content.

Sam: policy note: any customer-impacting incident that affects SLAs or has legal/compliance implications gets declared as an incident and Product gets looped in. Oncall should not try to 'suppress' notification to Product. If unsure, call me (page) and we'll assess within 15m.

Devon: nice. can we add some simple alert snippets to the runbook so routing is obvious? e.g.:
```
alert: high_token_latency
if: p95_token_latency > 500ms for 5m
route: runtime-oncall
severity: sev2
```
and
```
alert: host_gpu_ecc_errors
if: ecc_errors > 5 in 10m
route: sre-oncall
severity: sev1
```

Maria: please add both to the runbook. Also add a short checklist for whoever gets paged: 1) confirm scope (how many customers/routes), 2) check infra metrics (if SRE) / model metrics and KV cache hit rate (if runtime), 3) if >15m no resolution escalate to manager (Sam) and ping oncall-ops.

Devon: will do. one more: who pages marketing/support/CS for a regression that affects a small set of customers?

Sam: product & support notifications: if it's customer-visible (even small) and likely to trigger support tickets, Product owns outbound comms. Oncall should notify Product immediately with impact summary and any mitigations. We usually use the #incidnt-notify channel and the incident playbook template.

Lee: tiny operational suggestion: add a short table at top of runbook: "If alert contains tag: \"model-quality\" -> runtime; tag: \"infra-host\" -> sre; tag: \"unknown\" -> page sre + post to thread for runtime to join."

oncall-bot: reminder: please attach alert IDs to runbook entries and add the exact `pagerduty` escalation policy links. :bell: 

Devon: done — PR coming in ~30m to /docs/oncall/runbooks with those snippets and the matrix. I'll include a few real alert examples from last week.

Maria: awesome, thanks. Quick ask: can runtime add a small health check that reports KV cache size + hit-rate so SRE can see it in the alert dashboard? that'll speed triage.

Lee: yes — I'll open a task and tag infra to wire it into dashboard.

Sam: thanks team. This clarifies a ton. If anyone sees gaps once the PR lands ping me. :thumbsup:
